locator.text: Display 97.3, p. 97, in the proof of Lemma 8.7

evidence: paper: \int x^{p}\,\eta_j(x)\,dx \;=\; \mu_p\,e^{jdp},\qquad \mu_p \;=\; \int x^{p}\,\eta_0(x)\,dx \;>\; 0 \qquad\text{(with } \eta_j(x)=a_j^{-1}\eta_0(x/a_j),\ a_j=e^{jd},\ j=0,1,2,\ \eta_0\ge 0 \text{ a nonzero bump supported near } x_0>0\text{, from the sentence before the display)}

verdicts.summary:
Lean has an equivalent formula. The repository states the scaling identity in general form, but in the outgoing-pulse files, not in the Lemma 8.7 chain. `power_bump_integral_scale` (OutgoingPulseBounds.lean:543) gives, for every real a, every k > 0 and every 0 < l < u, ∫ t^a·bump(kl,ku)(t) dt = k·k^a·∫ t^a·bump(l,u)(t) dt, and `bump_scale` (:452) says bump(kl,ku)(kx) = bump(l,u)(x). Taking η_0 = bump(l,u) and η_j = k^{-1}·bump(kl,ku) = k^{-1}η_0(·/k) with k = e^{jd}, the first clause follows by pulling the constant k^{-1} out of the integral, k^{-1}·k·k^p = k^p, and (e^{jd})^p = e^{jdp}; this covers every real p, every j and every d. Conversely the Lean lemma is the display's computation for that particular bump with a general dilation factor.

The positivity clause is the weak point. For the same radial bump, μ_p > 0 is stated only for the template on (e^{-3/20}, e^{3/20}) and only for -1 ≤ p ≤ 0 (`rowMoment_bounds` :509 with `rowFloor_pos` :504); four of the paper's five exponents (2, -2-2λ, 1, 1-2λ) lie outside that range. What does follow by pure instantiation for every real p and every 0 < l < u is μ_p ≠ 0: `LocalizedMomentRepair.matrix_det_ne_zero` (LocalizedMomentRepair.lean:91) at n = 1, where the determinant is the single entry ∫ t^p·bump(l,u)(t). The strict sign for general p then needs only that the integral of a nonnegative integrand is nonnegative (`bump_nonneg` :31 and support in (l,u) with l > 0 are stated; the integral inequality is a Mathlib order fact, not a repository declaration). I counted that as sign bookkeeping, not as an unstated analytic estimate; a stricter reading would make this clause lean_weaker with severity low. The paper only uses μ_p as a nonzero row factor ("after dividing its rows by μ_p", and as the common row factors of A_θ, A_z on p. 98), so nonvanishing is what the later argument needs.

Independently, in the variable y = log x both clauses are stated for every real exponent: `AngularMomentReset.weighted_translate_integral` (:542, arbitrary f, shift and exponent), `bump_moment` (:97, the two-member family with step 2) and `moment_pos` (:88, 0 < moment s for all real s). Under x = e^y with η_0(x) = T(log x)/x this is the display with s = p, but passing between the two forms is a change of variables that I did not find stated for these functions (the nearest is `OutgoingSchedule.exp_weight_substitution` :635, on a finite interval), and the log template is a different function from the radial one, so I do not combine the two families.

Route difference, as A says: the Lean proof of Lemma 8.7 (`FiveRowRank.exists_five_row_repair` :311) never forms geometrically scaled copies. Its profiles are bumps on separated mesh cells (`cellLower`/`cellUpper`, FiveRowRank.lean:27-31), their moments stay unevaluated, and invertibility comes from `PowerMomentMatrix.bumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero` (PowerMomentMatrix.lean:261). That affects the neighbouring Vandermonde display, not whether this identity is in the repository. A's "absent" rests on having missed `power_bump_integral_scale`.
